items.text: Remark 4.2 (Comparison with $\kappa=2$ case). At $\kappa=2$, the spectrum in Eq. (11) recovers the original construction in [22]. More generally, if $A_{2}$ denotes the original precision matrix with the same rotation $O$, then $A=(\kappa-1)A_{2}-(\kappa-2)I_{d}$. Thus one matrix–vector reply for either matrix determines the corresponding reply for the other. The proof compares $\sum_{i}\cos(n\theta_{i})\langle x,Oe_{i}\rangle^{2}$ with $\|x\|^{2}$, where $n=2q+1$. For the output of a $q$-query algorithm, the ratio is at most $d^{-\Omega(1)}$ in absolute value (Lemma 4.4), whereas under the target the ratio of the means has absolute value $e^{-\Theta(n/\sqrt{\kappa})}$ (Lemma 4.5). Hence the test works for $n$ up to order $\sqrt{\kappa}\log d$, rather than $\log d$ as at $\kappa=2$, which is the source of the factor $\sqrt{\kappa}$ in Theorem 4.1.
